flow_trace.condition: The caller is engaging as the account holder / the person we are trying to reach — e.g. they answer affirmatively, give their name, say 'speaking' or 'that's me', or start providing any identifying detail. Fire this the moment the caller behaves like the right party. Do NOT fire ONLY if they explicitly say they are someone else, a third party, or that this is a wrong number (that case is handled by the other branch). When in doubt for a cooperative caller, FIRE — identity is still gated server-side by the verify_identity tool, so advancing here reveals nothing.
The person is not the borrower, is a third party, or says this is a wrong number.

analyzer_findings.detail: state advanced 'do_verify' -> 'wrap_up' but no declared transition connects them (and it is not a guard-fallback jump).
flow reached an end state but the simulated user's goal was NOT met (per the task-success judge).

states.goal: Greet the caller warmly and professionally on behalf of the business, and confirm you are speaking with the account holder by name. COMPLIANCE — this is mandatory and absolute: until identity is verified you may ONLY greet, ask to confirm you are speaking with the right person, and (if pressed) say you first need to confirm who you are speaking with. You MUST NOT state, confirm, deny, hint at, acknowledge, or discuss ANY debt, balance, amount, payment, account, loan, overdue status, or the reason for the call — not even to say there is or isn't one, and not even in general terms. If the caller asks why you are calling, do NOT answer the reason; say only that you first need to confirm who you are speaking with. If they confirm they are the account holder, move to identity verification. If they are someone else, a third party, or say it's a wrong number, reveal nothing about why you are calling.
states.label: Confirm right party

states.goal: Politely ask the caller for their full name AND ONE identifying detail: the last 4 digits of their account number OR their date of birth. ONE of those two is sufficient — the moment you have their name plus EITHER the last 4 digits OR a date of birth, you have everything you need: STOP asking, do NOT request the other factor, and do NOT ask any follow-up identity questions. Simply tell them you will confirm those details now. Take exactly what they say. Do NOT claim to have verified them and do NOT say they are already confirmed — once they have provided a name and one factor, the system runs the verification for you; your only job here is to collect those details accurately. COMPLIANCE — this is mandatory and absolute: until identity is verified you may ONLY ask for and take these identity details. You MUST NOT state, confirm, deny, hint at, acknowledge, or discuss ANY debt, balance, amount, payment, account detail, overdue status, or the purpose of the call here — verification comes first, with no exceptions. If asked why you are calling, say only that you must verify their identity first. If they outright refuse to give any identity detail, disclose nothing and close respectfully.
states.label: Collect identity details

states.goal: Identity is now confirmed, so you may now disclose. Explain that you are calling from the business about an overdue payment on their account. State that our records show ₹{{due_amount}} due, {{days_overdue}} days past the due date ({{due_date}}) — present it as what our records show, not a confirmed live balance. Use lookup_record only if they ask for the live balance or their last payment. If they mention an updated phone number or email during the conversation, capture it with save_contact_field. Then work toward resolution: listen and understand their situation before responding. Never threaten, shame, or imply legal action.
states.label: Disclose balance

states.goal: The borrower is willing and able to pay now. Confirm the mobile number to send to, then generate a secure payment link (payment_link) and send it by SMS (send_sms). Tell them the link is on its way and how to complete the payment. Never claim the link is sent unless the tool confirms it.
states.label: Pay now

states.goal: The borrower needs more time. Ask for a SPECIFIC promise-to-pay date, repeat it back to confirm, and record it with capture_ptp and schedule_followup. Tell them you have noted the date and the team will follow up — do NOT promise that an automated call will be placed. Offer schedule_callback if they prefer a call back at a set time. Do not push for payment more than twice.
states.label: Promise to pay

states.goal: This is not the account holder. Apologize briefly for the interruption. Do NOT reveal the reason for the call or any account detail to a third party. Politely ask when the account holder might be reachable and capture an alternate number with capture_alternate_number if offered. If they ask not to be called again, honor it with stop_calling. Then close politely.
states.label: Wrong / third party

states.goal: Confirm the agreed next step out loud so nothing is ambiguous — payment link sent, the promise-to-pay date, or a scheduled callback, whichever applies. If identity was never verified, do NOT reveal or hint at any debt, balance, amount, account, or the reason for the call — simply thank them for their time and close respectfully. Otherwise, if nothing could be agreed, leave the easy payment option open once more, then stop. Thank them for their time and close professionally and respectfully.
states.label: Confirm & close

transitions.condition: The caller is engaging as the account holder / the person we are trying to reach — e.g. they answer affirmatively, give their name, say 'speaking' or 'that's me', or start providing any identifying detail. Do NOT fire ONLY if they explicitly say they are someone else, a third party, or that this is a wrong number (that case is handled by the other branch). When in doubt for a cooperative caller, FIRE — identity is still gated server-side by the verify_identity tool, so advancing here reveals nothing.
The person is not the borrower, is a third party, or says this is a wrong number.

DETERMINISTIC: after the caller has responded in the collect state, always attempt the server-side verify_identity check on the details in context. This must NOT be an LLM judgement — a judge under-fires and a cooperative caller then never reaches do_verify. The forced verify tool fails closed (loops back here to re-ask, bounded by max_visits_per_state → wrap_up) unless the name plus last-4/DOB actually match, and it opens the identity_verified gate the moment they do.
The borrower is willing and able to pay now.
The borrower cannot pay right now but is willing to pay later / needs time.
The borrower disputes the debt, says it is already paid, describes hardship beyond the agent's authority, or asks to speak with a person.
The borrower clearly refuses to pay or discuss further after the easy option has been offered.
